items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline; a touch softer and more serious for the line about the lakes vanishing. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: Almost every lake you see in Bengaluru... was built by hand.
Over eleven hundred years. Then the city lost most of them.
So why build lakes at all?
Look at the map. Bengaluru sits on a ridge, about nine hundred and twenty metres up.
No big river flows here. Rivers run downhill... Bengaluru IS the hill.
So how do you fill lakes... with no river?
People built earth walls across the valleys, to trap the rain.
Rain fills one lake. It spills into the next. Then the next.
[giddy little raindrop, squeaky, sliding fast, delighted] Wheee! Lake number seven!
Canals linked them into six chains, stepping down three valleys.
In fifteen thirty-seven, Kempay-gowda founded the city... and kept building more.
Then the city grew. And grew. And grew.
From nineteen seventy-three to twenty thirteen, about seventy-nine percent of its water bodies vanished.
So today, water is pumped about a hundred kilometres from the Kaveri... and lifted three hundred metres uphill.
The city that built its own lakes... now borrows a river.
And the lost lakes? Many are hiding in plain sight.
[deadpan, tired old city bus, low and slow, matter-of-fact] Technically... I'm parked in a lake.
Bengaluru never had a big river. So it made lakes instead.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
